proposals.evidence: Electrical characteristics: "Reverse recovery time IF = IR = 10 mA, iR = 1 mA trr ... 8 ns" (max); second row "IF = 10 mA, VR = 6 V, iR = 0.1 x IR, RL = 100 ohm ... 4 ns" (max)
proposals.method: Charge-control storage-time estimate used by the SPICE lumped-charge diode: ts = TT*ln(1+IF/IR). Treating the whole quoted trr as storage time gives TT = trr/ln(1+IF/IR). Ignores the recovery tail to the quoted Irr, junction capacitance and RS, so it over-estimates TT. With IF=IR=10 mA: TT <= 8 ns/ln 2 = 11.5 ns. This is an UPPER BOUND from a maximum trr, not a typical value; the 4 ns row has an ill-defined IR (set by 6 V/100 ohm) and gives a weaker bound. The class default TT 23 ns that this entry currently inherits would give ts ~16 ns, which exceeds the 8 ns maximum.

proposals.evidence: "Breakdown voltage IR = 100 uA, tp/T = 0.01, tp = 0.3 ms V(BR) 100" (MIN column)
proposals.method: Minimum breakdown at IR=100 uA; pair with IBV=100 uA. A guaranteed minimum, not a typical breakdown.
